transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-03-01
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Summit Head of AI), Daniel Ortiz (VP Engineering), Nisha Patel (Security), Omar Reyes (SRE)

Summary: renewal + expansion check-in. Summit is mid-renewal and evaluating capacity upgrades and EU region support. Security asks for SOC2/KMS details. SE to run benchmark against peak QPS.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone good to see you all, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side - I'm Jordan, account lead, and Priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Laura Kim: Hi, Laura here, thanks. We'll be pretty focused today on capacity and the EU region ask.
[00:25] Daniel Ortiz: Daniel - timeline is we need to lock terms in the next two weeks.
[00:30] Priya Nair: Great, thanks. So high level from Summit's notes we saw your current usage and you're trending up, looking to bump reserved capacity and add EU region - right?
[00:42] Laura: Yep, that's right. Our traffic spiked during end-of-month processing, latency was a bit higher, and ops wants dedicated capacity to stabilize p50/p95.
[00:53] Jordan: Makes sense. On the renewal side you were on a 6-month term - you're evaluating a 12-month extension with a 50% capacity uplift and adding EU for GDPR/data residency. Is that fair?
[01:06] Daniel: That's the ask. Also want to understand cost delta for dedicated vs hosted with VPC.
[01:12] Nisha Patel: And from security, we need SOC2, audit logs retention options, and KMS integration - HSM in particular if possible.
[01:20] Priya: Totally. On dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and optional burst capacity. For EU region we can provision dedicated nodes in eu-west-1 - and we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments; for hosted we have envelope encryption and partner KMS options.
[01:37] Omar Reyes: When you say burst capacity what's the latency profile when bursting from reserved to burst nodes? We can't have p95 jump more than 60ms ideally.
[01:45] Priya: Good question. In our experience burst is designed for throughput, and we keep fallback routing so short-lived bursts route to compatible variants. Typical p95 delta is implementation dependent - we'll run benchmarks with your payload to show expected p50/p95.
[02:02] Jordan: We'll propose a benchmarking window that simulates end-of-month traffic. Priya will run it.

[02:35] Laura: On pricing - can you share the delta for 12 months vs monthly? We're trying to justify budget to finance.
[02:42] Jordan: Yes - we can offer a committed rate for the 12-month term with a tiered discount at 30% committed usage, and deeper discounts for the 50% uplift. I'll send an updated term sheet.
[02:52] Daniel: Do you have a calculator or spreadsheet? We need per-token and per-embedding numbers and expected monthly spend.
[02:58] Jordan: We'll attach a pricing spreadsheet with samples. It will include per-token pricing, reserved node pricing, and estimated cost after auto-batching/kv-cache effects.

[03:20] Priya: A few technical notes - we observed your request sizes are long, KV cache hit rate could help a lot. Also quantization profiles we suggested earlier - switching to 4-bit helped similar customers reduce GPU memory and cost, with small accuracy tradeoffs.
[03:36] Laura: We're a bit nervous about quantization impact on outputs for compliance-sensitive communications.
[03:42] Priya: Completely understandable. We can run A/B evals on your prompt sets to quantify regressions. Redwood Optimize also surfaces model/quant profiles by workload - but we'll validate with your evals.

[04:10] Nisha: For SOC2, do you have a recent report and an option for longer audit log retention? Our compliance team requires 12 months of immutable logs.
[04:18] Jordan: Yes we have a SOC2 Type II report, and retention options are configurable - we can offer longer retention as an add-on. I'll attach the SOC2 and the retention options doc.
[04:26] Nisha: And KMS - can you support customer-managed keys in EU for private deployment?
[04:30] Priya: For private deployments - yes, you can bring your KMS/HSM. For hosted we support BYOK integration through a partner KMS flow, but for strict residency you might prefer the Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment.

[05:05] Omar: Any changes required on our side to route traffic to a dedicated pool? We use an internal gateway and expect sticky sessions for KV cache locality.
[05:13] Priya: We'll provide network config guides. Sticky routing is supported via session tokens, and Prefetch/Prefix caching is available to preserve KV locality. We'll work with your SRE to configure.

[06:00] Laura: One sensitivity - we have EU customers and need data never to leave EU. If you spin up eu nodes does logs or telemetry cross regions?
[06:08] Jordan: Nothing crosses regions if you select the EU-only option - control plane metadata can be region-restricted with Private deployments. We'll document the exact data flows - Priya will follow up.

[07:00] Priya: For the benchmark we're proposing: 2-hour test, ramp to your peak QPS, measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost. We'll try 3 model variants: default open model, quantized variant, and a lower-latency smaller model for fallback.
[07:18] Daniel: That sounds good. We'll provide histograms and sample prompts - Omar will send those after the call.
[07:24] Omar: Yep, I'll drop them in the playbook repo.

[08:00] Laura: On contract terms - any flexibility on early termination or overage? We want predictable spend if we commit for 12 months.
[08:09] Jordan: For committed terms we offer monthly true-ups and some overage protection tiers. We can add a cap for the first quarter as part of the negotiation. I'll include options in the term sheet.

[08:30] Nisha: A couple of security questions: do you support SAML/SSO for RBAC and can we get org-level audit trails by user?
[08:38] Priya: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported and we provide user-level audit logs. Retention and export formats are configurable.

[09:00] Daniel: Any competitors we should be worried about for latency at scale? We've run some quick tests with Vertex and saw similar p50 but different cost.
[09:08] Jordan: Some customers compare us to Anthropic/OpenAI and cloud providers. We try to differentiate on predictable serving economics and the routing/fallbacks - plus the dedicated pools and observability. We'll share comparative benchmarks but will emphasize your benchmark.

[10:00] Priya: Quick note on routing - we can route by latency or cost. For critical workflows you can pin model versions and use auto-fallback if capacity is constrained. That keeps SLAs intact.

[12:00] Laura: Does the EU deployment add a significant lead time? We need it online before quarterly close - ~3 weeks.
[12:08] Jordan: We usually provision EU dedicated pools in 2-3 weeks depending on capacity. With a committed order we can expedite.

[14:00] Omar: How do we validate throughput for end-of-month bursts? Will the benchmark include realistic caching warms?
[14:10] Priya: Yes - we'll include warm-up and steady-state phases and measure caching effects. We'll also run a cold and warm cache scenario so you see differences.

[17:00] Jordan: I'll follow up with the term sheet and pricing spreadsheet. Priya will schedule the benchmark run once she receives the sample prompts and histograms. Nisha will get the SOC2 and KMS docs.

[20:00] Nisha: One more quick one - do you support per-route rate limits and token-level cost attribution for internal teams?
[20:08] Priya: Yes we do per-route analytics and token-level breakdowns in the console. You can set per-route budgets and alerting.

[24:00] Laura: Okay that's helpful. Anything else on the EU data residency?
[24:06] Jordan: Just to reiterate - for strict residency we'd recommend Private or Dedicated EU nodes with BYOK. We'll document data flows and network boundaries.

[28:00] Daniel: From finance standpoint, what's the delta if we go 24-months? Is there a meaningful discount vs 12?
[28:06] Jordan: Yes we can push a 24-month option with extra discount tiers - I'll include that in the term sheet.

[32:00] Priya: Small technical ask - can your SREs provide a sample of the largest prompt and average token length? That helps with memory/kv-cache sizing.
[32:08] Omar: I'll include top-10 and histograms in the repo.

[36:00] Laura: Let's recap next steps so we can move quickly.
[36:06] Jordan: Recap: Jordan send pricing/term sheet + SOC2 doc by 2027-03-04. Priya to schedule and run a 2-hour benchmark and share results by 2027-03-06. Summit to provide payloads and histograms by 2027-03-03. Follow-up call 2027-03-08 to finalize contract.
[36:30] Nisha: That works.
[36:35] Daniel: Works for engineering as well.
[36:40] Laura: Thanks everyone.
[36:45] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments and next steps.

[44:30] End of meeting: informal wrap, small chitchat, meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hears present (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash") and occasional speaker switching. This is an auto-transcript; SE and AE provided clarifications during call.
